reason: Translucent (pellucid) dots in leaflets and leaf blades are internal oil glands seen against the light, which is what gland-dotted means. 'Without translucent dots' is the negated value.

label: subpercurrent
definition: A positional quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's extending through most of the structure through which it runs but ending below its apex.
reason: This is the standard costa character in moss floras. It sits beside percurrent (FLOPO:0991163) and excurrent (FLOPO:0991162). 'Not percurrent' would be wrong because it also covers excurrent.

This says a part (the nectary scale over the nectary pit) is absent. PO has no nectary scale class, and the bare word 'scale' was rejected as a generic part, so a bearer class is needed before this can be a rule:entity_absence.
Says whether the flower (or a fruit valve) opens fully at anthesis. 'Widely' is a degree of open; 'not opening widely' is the negated value.
This is a tissue, not a quality. Where the record's part is a stem, use stem cortex (PO_0025612). The layer counts that follow go to the count pattern.
This is a character heading, not a value. The values under it (lisse, striée, lenticellée) are covered by their own terms and rules.
Clathrate scales and septa have cells whose thick walls form a lattice. That fits reticulate, whose definition says 'composed of a network of veins, ridges or walls'.

This is a compound word with the part built in: the petiole (PO_0020038) of the leaf is winged. The bearer is the petiole, not the leaf.

label: pachymorph
definition: A shape quality inhering in a rhizome by virtue of its being short and thick, each segment curving upwards and ending in an aerial shoot, so that the shoots arise in a clump.
reason: A real bamboo and grass rhizome type that PATO does not have. Its opposite is leptomorph (long, thin, running rhizomes).
This mixes erumpent warts with capsules that break open irregularly. Neither fits dehiscent (FLOPO:0991149), which requires a definite line, and PATO:0040044 ruptured means damage.
An anthelate inflorescence is an anthela. PO has that class (with synonym anthela), so the word names the bearer class, not a quality.
'With trichomes' says hairs are present, the same way lenticellate maps to lenticel present (rule C204). The quality-side equivalent is PATO_0000454 hairy.
This is the definition of FLOPO:0991101: members of a set of like parts differing in size.

label: longitudinally dehiscent
definition: A dehiscent quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's opening by a slit that runs along its length.
reason: The commonest anther dehiscence type. It sits beside poricidal (FLOPO:0991153) and the other children of dehiscent.
States that glands are present. Gland maps to PO_0005656 (rule C265), and 'sin glándulas' is the absence form.
Diminutive plants, leaves or inflorescences are very small, i.e. small for their kind.
A discoid stigma. 'Thickly' only qualifies how thick the disc is and does not need its own term.
This negates spotted.

target: new: size gradient along a series
reason: This describes how size changes along a series of like parts (leaflets, bracts, buds from apex to base). That is a relation between parts by position, not a value of one part.
Terete means circular in cross section. This is the usual use for scapes, branchlets and pedicels.

label: obtrulloid
definition: A convex 3-D shape quality inhering in a bearer by virtue of the bearer's being a solid whose longitudinal section is obtrullate: widest above the middle, with straight sides converging to the base.
reason: The solid counterpart of obtrullate (FLOPO:0991353), in the same way obpyriform and barrel-shaped sit under convex 3-D shape. Used for carpels, seeds and spikes.
Follows rule C181 (expanded filament base = dilated). The quality belongs to the base of the filament, petiole or style.

In moss capsules this means a distinct apophysis is present, and PO_0030040 lists 'apophysis' as a synonym. The hypanthium uses ('basally apophysate') may instead mean a swollen base and need checking.

target: new: size gradient along a series
reason: Graded involucral bracts or teeth get gradually longer from the outer series to the inner (or along the margin). This is the same series-gradient relation as 'decreasing in size'.
Vague and not a quality on its own. In the examples it is a fragment of a position phrase.
Marginate is already a synonym of margined. 'Narrowly' describes the width of the band and does not need its own term.

word: ratio of second sinus/middle segment length
reason: This is a numeric ratio between the depth of one sinus and the length of a segment, two different parts. That is the ratio-to-another-part pattern, not a quality term.
Net-veined is already an exact synonym of reticulate, which covers calyces, fruit valves and seed coats marked by a network of veins.
